Objective: Check that a new user can sign up with a unique email.
Prerequisites: A unique email not already used.
Test Steps: 1. Open register page. 2. Enter name, email, and password. 3. Click Create account.
Expected Result: Account is created and user goes to dashboard.

Objective: Check that name is required while creating account.
Test Steps: 1. Open register page. 2. Leave name empty. 3. Fill email and password. 4. Click Create account.
Expected Result: Name is required message is shown.

Objective: Check that email is required while creating account.
Test Steps: 1. Open register page. 2. Fill name and password. 3. Leave email empty. 4. Click Create account.
Expected Result: Email is required message is shown.

Objective: Check that wrong email format is rejected.
Test Steps: 1. Open register page. 2. Enter abc as email. 3. Fill other fields. 4. Submit.
Expected Result: Email must be valid message is shown.

Objective: Check that short password is rejected.
Test Steps: 1. Open register page. 2. Enter password less than 6 characters. 3. Submit.
Expected Result: Password must be at least 6 characters message is shown.

Objective: Check that same email cannot be registered again.
Prerequisites: A user already exists with same email.
Test Steps: 1. Open register page. 2. Enter existing email. 3. Submit form.
Expected Result: Email already in use error is shown.

Objective: Check that password is not saved as plain text.
Test Steps: 1. Open MySQL Workbench. 2. Run select query on users table. 3. Check password column.
Expected Result: Password is saved as BCrypt hash.

Objective: Check that registered user can login.
Test Steps: 1. Open login page. 2. Enter correct email and password. 3. Click Continue.
Expected Result: Login succeeds and user goes to dashboard.

Objective: Make sure wrong password is rejected.
Test Steps: 1. Open login page. 2. Enter valid email. 3. Type wrong password. 4. Click Continue.
Expected Result: Login fails and error is shown.

Objective: Check that email is required on login.
Test Steps: 1. Open login page. 2. Leave email blank. 3. Enter password. 4. Submit.
Expected Result: Email is required message is shown.

Objective: Check that password is required on login.
Test Steps: 1. Open login page. 2. Enter email. 3. Leave password blank. 4. Submit.
Expected Result: Password is required message is shown.

Objective: Check invalid email on login page.
Test Steps: 1. Open login page. 2. Enter abc in email field. 3. Enter password. 4. Submit.
Expected Result: Email must be valid message is shown or browser blocks submit.
Comments: LoginRequest has @Email and input type is email.

Objective: Check login error when backend is not running.
Test Steps: 1. Open login page. 2. Enter any details. 3. Click Continue.
Expected Result: Backend server is not running on port 8081 message is shown.

Objective: Verify user stays logged in after refresh.
Test Steps: 1. Open dashboard. 2. Refresh browser.
Expected Result: User stays logged in and dashboard opens again.

Objective: Check invalid token removes session.
Prerequisites: Invalid token is stored in localStorage.
Test Steps: 1. Add wrong token in localStorage. 2. Refresh app or open protected page.
Expected Result: User is redirected to login and storage is cleared.

Objective: Check that token is sent with backend requests.
Test Steps: 1. Open profile page. 2. Check network request headers.
Expected Result: Authorization header contains Bearer token.

Objective: Check protected route for dashboard.
Test Steps: 1. Directly open /dashboard.
Expected Result: User is sent to /login.

Objective: Check protected route for profile page.
Test Steps: 1. Directly open /profile.
Expected Result: User is sent to /login.
Comments: Profile route is wrapped with ProtectedRoute.

Objective: Check logout button clears user session.
Test Steps: 1. Click Logout button from navbar.
Expected Result: Token and user are removed and login page opens.

Objective: Check forgot password page opens from login.
Test Steps: 1. Open login page. 2. Click Forgot password link.
Expected Result: Forgot password page is displayed.

Objective: Check reset link generation for existing email.
Prerequisites: A registered email exists. Mail may not be configured.
Test Steps: 1. Open forgot password page. 2. Enter registered email. 3. Click Send reset link.
Expected Result: Reset message is shown. If mail is not configured, reset link is shown on page.
Comments: AuthServiceImpl.forgotPassword returns resetLink when mail config is missing.

Objective: Check app does not reveal if email exists.
Prerequisites: Use an email not present in database.
Test Steps: 1. Open forgot password page. 2. Enter unknown email. 3. Submit.
Expected Result: Generic reset message is shown.
Comments: AuthServiceImpl returns same reset message for unknown email.

Objective: Check reset page behavior without token.
Test Steps: 1. Open /reset-password without token.
Expected Result: Update password button is disabled.
Comments: ResetPasswordPage disables button when token is missing.

Objective: Check confirm password validation.
Prerequisites: Reset page has token in URL.
Test Steps: 1. Enter different password and confirm password. 2. Submit.
Expected Result: Passwords do not match message is shown.
Comments: ResetPasswordPage checks password and confirmPassword before API call.

Objective: Check short password during reset.
Test Steps: 1. Enter password less than 6 characters. 2. Submit.
Expected Result: Password must be at least 6 characters message is shown.

Objective: Check invalid reset token is rejected.
Test Steps: 1. Open reset page with wrong token. 2. Enter valid password. 3. Submit.
Expected Result: Password reset link is invalid or expired message is shown.
Comments: AuthServiceImpl.resetPassword checks hashed reset token and expiry.

Test Case Name: Login Lockout After Many Wrong Attempts
Objective: Check if account locks after many failed logins.
Test Steps: 1. Enter wrong password many times. 2. Observe result.
Expected Result: Account lock or captcha should appear if implemented.
Comments: No lockout or captcha code exists.

Objective: Check logged in user can open profile page.
Test Steps: 1. Click Profile from navbar.
Expected Result: Profile page opens with user details.

Objective: Check profile details are visible.
Test Steps: 1. Open profile page. 2. Check left profile card.
Expected Result: Name, email, user id, joined date, and last updated date are shown.
Comments: ProfileResponse returns userId, name, email, role, createdAt, updatedAt.

Objective: Check loading text while profile is loading.
Test Steps: 1. Open profile page. 2. Observe screen before data loads.
Expected Result: Loading profile... is displayed.

Objective: Check user can update name.
Test Steps: 1. Open profile page. 2. Change full name. 3. Click Save changes.
Expected Result: Profile updated message is shown and new name appears.

Objective: Check user can update email.
Prerequisites: User is logged in. New email is unique.
Test Steps: 1. Open profile page. 2. Change email. 3. Save changes.
Expected Result: Email updates and user remains logged in.
Comments: AuthServiceImpl.updateProfile returns new JWT token after email update.

Objective: Check name validation on profile update.
Test Steps: 1. Open profile page. 2. Clear full name. 3. Save changes.
Expected Result: Name is required message is shown.

Objective: Check email validation on profile update.
Test Steps: 1. Open profile page. 2. Clear email. 3. Save changes.
Expected Result: Email is required message is shown.

Objective: Check invalid email on profile update.
Test Steps: 1. Enter wrong email format. 2. Save changes.
Expected Result: Email must be valid message is shown or browser blocks submit.

Objective: Check user cannot use another user email.
Test Steps: 1. Login as first user. 2. Enter second user email in profile. 3. Save.
Expected Result: Email already in use error is shown.

Objective: Check password can be changed from profile.
Prerequisites: User is logged in and knows current password.
Test Steps: 1. Enter current password. 2. Enter new password. 3. Click Save changes. 4. Logout and login with new password.
Expected Result: Password changes and login works with new password.
Comments: AuthServiceImpl checks current password before encoding new password.

Test Case Name: Change Password With Wrong Current Password
Objective: Check wrong current password is rejected.
Test Steps: 1. Enter wrong current password. 2. Enter new password. 3. Save.
Expected Result: Current password is incorrect error is shown.

Objective: Check current password is required for password change.
Test Steps: 1. Leave current password empty. 2. Enter new password. 3. Save.
Expected Result: Current password is incorrect error is shown.
Comments: Backend rejects newPassword when currentPassword is empty.

Objective: Check new password minimum length.
Test Steps: 1. Enter current password. 2. Enter new password less than 6 characters. 3. Save.
Expected Result: New password must be at least 6 characters message is shown.

Objective: Check name/email update works without password fields.
Test Steps: 1. Edit name or email. 2. Leave password fields blank. 3. Save.
Expected Result: Profile updates and old password still works.
Comments: Password is changed only if newPassword has text.

Objective: Check reset button restores form.
Test Steps: 1. Change name and email in form. 2. Click Reset.
Expected Result: Name and email return to saved values and password fields clear.
Comments: ProfilePage.jsx reset button uses emptyForm and profile values.

Objective: Check eye button for current password.
Test Steps: 1. Type current password. 2. Click eye button.
Expected Result: Password becomes visible. Clicking again hides it.

Objective: Check eye button for new password.
Test Steps: 1. Type new password. 2. Click eye button.
Expected Result: Password becomes visible. Clicking again hides it.

Objective: Check profile page on small screen.
Test Steps: 1. Open profile page. 2. Resize browser to mobile width.
Expected Result: Profile sections stack one below another.

Objective: Check dashboard opens after successful login.
Test Steps: 1. Login with valid user.
Expected Result: Dashboard page opens.

Objective: Check user name is shown on home page.
Test Steps: 1. Open dashboard. 2. Check hero section.
Expected Result: Good day, user name is displayed.

Objective: Check Browse products button.
Test Steps: 1. Click Browse products button.
Expected Result: Products page opens.

Objective: Check Products card navigation.
Test Steps: 1. Click Products card.
Expected Result: Products page opens.

Objective: Check My cart card navigation.
Test Steps: 1. Click My cart card.
Expected Result: Cart page opens.
Comments: My cart card has onClick navigate(/cart).

Objective: Check Orders card navigation.
Test Steps: 1. Click Orders card.
Expected Result: Orders page should open if card is clickable.
Comments: Orders card has no onClick in DashboardPage.jsx.

Objective: Check Home link from navbar.
Test Steps: 1. Click Home in navbar.
Expected Result: Dashboard opens and Home link is active.

Objective: Check Mercato logo navigation.
Test Steps: 1. Click Mercato logo in navbar.
Expected Result: Dashboard opens.

Objective: Check normal user cannot see admin link.
Prerequisites: Logged in user role is USER.
Test Steps: 1. Open dashboard. 2. Check navbar.
Expected Result: Admin Panel link is not visible.
Comments: Navbar shows Admin Panel only for ADMIN role.

Objective: Check admin can see admin link.
Prerequisites: Logged in user role is ADMIN.
Test Steps: 1. Open dashboard. 2. Check navbar.
Expected Result: Admin Panel link is visible.

Objective: Check cart count in navbar.
Test Steps: 1. Open dashboard. 2. Check Cart link in navbar.
Expected Result: Cart badge shows item count when count is more than zero.
Comments: Navbar.jsx calls getCart and shows badge when cartCount > 0.

Objective: Check dashboard on mobile screen.
Test Steps: 1. Open dashboard. 2. Resize screen below 800px.
Expected Result: Cards show in one column and heading becomes smaller.

Objective: Check footer on home page.
Test Steps: 1. Open dashboard. 2. Scroll to footer.
Expected Result: Footer is visible. Brand text currently shows ShopApp.
Comments: Footer.jsx has ShopApp while app branding is Mercato.
